images.caption:
The Hippodrome was first built around 203 by the Roman Emperor Septimus Severus.  It was greatly expanded by Emperor Constantine sometime after 324, after he made Byzantium (Constantinople) the capital of the Roman Empire.  The Hippodrome was used for horse and charior races, and could hold 100,000 spectators.  It was about 450 m (1,475 ft) long and 130 m (430 ft) wide.  

The Obelisk of Thutmose III is in the center of the photo.  It was brought from Karnak, Egypt, by Emperor Theodosius in 390.  It was created in 1490 BC.  It is 19 m (62 ft) high, 25 m (82 ft) including the base.  The Serpent Column is inside the fence at center left.  It was dedicated to the gods after the Greeks defeated the Perisians in the Battle of Platea, in 479 BC.
